text: An AI agent buys a seven-cent article. Paying for it through PayPal today costs forty-nine cents in fees.
And a reader who wants one article is asked to buy a whole subscription. So small purchases never happen.
UnitMarket fixes that. Buy just what you need, let agents pay in cents, and let PayPal settle.
Here is the working app. A reader says what they need, and what they will pay.
The app searches only authorised offers, and proposes a pack within budget, here from two publishers.
Nothing is charged until the reader approves. The price is frozen, and each publisher gets its own PayPal payment.
This take runs in dry run, on a pretend PayPal. The same code made real PayPal sandbox payments on the twenty-ninth of October.
Access opens only after the payment is verified. Receipt, library, done.

Now hand that power to an agent. Through our API, the buyer sets a one-time cap: five dollars, and three purchases. An operator, with a second factor, switches agent buying on. The agent buys on its own, and the cap stops it.
Agents buy in five to ten cent pieces. Here are ten thousand simulated trades, from a hundred agents and forty publishers.

Paid one by one, the fees come to four thousand nine hundred dollars, six times what was bought. Our ledger nets the trades into a hundred and ninety-eight PayPal movements: eighty-three dollars, fifty-nine times cheaper at today's prices. At a micro-settlement price we propose to PayPal: twenty-one dollars.
Pillars one and two are consolidation.

Buyers who want the same unit share one payment: ten thousand payments become two hundred and thirty-three. Small publishers pool on a topic to fill bundles none could fill alone: thirty-three of thirty-three, and they earn, instead of losing money to fees.
Behind it: two repositories, three hundred and thirty-five thousand lines of TypeScript, more than fourteen thousand tests, and eighty-one merged pull requests.
Four roles, ten buyer personas, forty content domains, tested end to end.
UnitMarket does the matching. PayPal stays the rails.
Every scene is labelled: real sandbox, dry run, simulation, or proposal.
Group the demand. Group the supply. Make cents worth paying. That is a ride-hailing model for payments, and we want to build it with PayPal. We built the proof.
UnitMarket. PayPal settles. We make cents worth paying.
